text.p: Lehman Brothers said in a report released on Thursday it was raising its 1997 earnings estimates for Israel's Orbotech Ltd.

Analyst Ted Kundtz said he is now expected 1997 EPS to reach $1.81 from his previous $1.72 and initiated a 1998 forecast of $2.13 for the maker of automated optical inspection equipment for making printed circuit boards (PCBs) and other devices.

"We came away from a recent meeting...comfortable that the company is on course for another stellar earnings year, paced by continued strength in the PCB equipment business and an impressive recovery of the flat panel display inspection equipment area," Kundtz said.

He said Orbotech's stock price was "attractively valued", trading at 9.7 times prospective 1997 earnings and gave the share a one-year target price of $25. Orbotech's Nasdaq stock was trading at 19 3/8 on Thursday morning.
Kundtz added that with $46.6 million in cash and no debt, Orbotech was in a position to make strategic acquisitions.
